nipponopelta:study:1.title: A new nodosaurid ankylosaur (Dinosauria: Ornithischia) from the Upper Cretaceous Hikagenosawa Formation in Japan reveals dispersal pattern of Asian nodosaurid ankylosaurs (Cretaceous Research, 2027)

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Nipponopelta was discovered by Eijiro Goto on June 25, 1995, in Yūbari, Hokkaido, Japan.
facts.quote: The Nipponopelta fossil material was discovered by Eijiro Goto on June 25, 1995, along the bank of the Omakizawa River in the city of Yūbari in Hokkaido, Japan.

facts.statement: The fossil was found inside a calcareous concretion that had eroded from the Hikagenosawa Formation.
facts.quote: The partial skull of an ankylosaur was preserved within a calcareous concretion that had eroded from outcrops of the Hikagenosawa Formation.

facts.statement: The fossil was donated to the Mikasa City Museum and accessioned as specimen MCM A522.
facts.quote: Goto donated the fossil to the Mikasa City Museum, where it was permanently accessioned as specimen MCM A522.

facts.statement: Nipponopelta was formally described as a new genus and species in 2026 by Shumpei Oyabu and colleagues, with MCM A522 designated as the holotype.
facts.quote: In 2026, Shumpei Oyabu and colleagues described Nipponopelta yezoensis as a new genus and species of nodosaurid ankylosaur based on these fossil remains, designating MCM A522 as the holotype specimen.

facts.statement: The known fossil material includes the rear part of a skull, disarticulated teeth, the first cervical vertebra, and two armor plates.
facts.quote: The material they could observe included the rear portion of the skull (the front part being missing), several disarticulated teeth, the atlas (first cervical vertebra), and two osteoderms (armor plates).

facts.statement: The genus name combines the Japanese word for Japan with the Greek word for shield.
facts.quote: The generic name, Nipponopelta, combines the Japanese word 日本 (Nippon), meaning Japan, with the Greek word πέλτη (péltē), meaning shield.

facts.statement: The species name refers to Yezo, the traditional name for Hokkaido, the location of the discovery.
facts.quote: The specific name, yezoensis, alludes to Yezo, the traditional name for Hokkaido, where the only known specimen was discovered.

facts.statement: Nipponopelta is classified as a member of the family Nodosauridae.
facts.quote: A member of the family Nodosauridae.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Nipponopelta within the Nodosaurinae subfamily, closer to Nodosaurus and Panoplosaurus than to Polacanthus or Struthiosaurus.
facts.quote: Nipponopelta was recovered as a derived member of the Nodosauridae, more closely related to Nodosaurus and Panoplosaurus (Nodosaurinae) than to Polacanthus (Polacanthinae) or Struthiosaurus (Struthiosauridae).

facts.statement: Nipponopelta lived during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically the Cenomanian age.
The estimated time range for Nipponopelta is between 100.5 and 93.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Cenomanian (100.5 to 93.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: The genus is known from the Upper Cretaceous Hikagenosawa Formation of the Yezo Group in Japan.
facts.quote: Nipponopelta () is an extinct genus of nodosaurid ankylosaurian dinosaur known from the Upper Cretaceous (Cenomanian age) Hikagenosawa Formation of the Yezo Group in Japan.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that Nipponopelta likely inhabited near-marine environments such as coastal and estuarine areas.
facts.quote: In their description of this taxon, Oyabu and colleagues suggested that Nipponopelta and its close relatives favored near-marine settings like coastal and estuarine environments.

facts.statement: Scientists note that the presence of nodosaurid fossils in marine deposits might be partly due to the transport of carcasses after death.
facts.quote: However, they acknowledged that the frequent occurrence of nodosaurid remains in marine deposits could be partially explained by post-mortem transport of carcasses.

facts.statement: It is debated whether nodosaurid fossils found in marine deposits represent the actual habitat of the animals or result from post-mortem transport.
facts.quote: However, they acknowledged that the frequent occurrence of nodosaurid remains in marine deposits could be partially explained by post-mortem transport of carcasses.
